<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1081
Claimant:
Benjamin Nash
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
03/12/2025
First notice of loss received from the insured driver reporting a low-speed head-on collision with another vehicle
earlier today. The claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
04/03/2025
Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file
suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start date.
04/21/2025
Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and matches the reported
sequence of events. Responding officers and a witness statement are consistent with this.
06/04/2025
Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward
beyond those already noted, so the photos and the report are the main sources for the event.
08/12/2025
Vehicle damage was inspected and matches the described impact direction and speed. The file shows no earlier
damage to this vehicle in prior claims or inspection records.
08/20/2025
Claimant's reported neck strain is plausible for a collision of this type. Medical records show a small strain to the
same area several years ago that fully healed, which is noted for context.
08/28/2025
Claimant's account has remained the same in every conversation with the adjuster and counsel, including the initial
statement and the follow-up call.
09/11/2025
Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injruy and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records show
steady progress with no unexplained gaps in care.
10/23/2025
Reviewed the file with the supervisor. The injury, treatment, and vehicle damage are consistent with the reported loss,
and the claim will proceed to evaluation with counsel's demand package.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
